bib.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning

question: Can language agents learn from trial and error without weight updates by turning task feedback into verbal self-reflections stored in an episodic memory?
hypothesis: Verbal self-reflection stored in memory acts as a semantic gradient that improves an agent over successive trials on decision-making, reasoning and coding tasks.
contributions: Reflexion, a paradigm for verbal reinforcement that parameterizes a policy as an agent's memory encoding paired with a choice of LLM parameters
Empirical evidence that self-reflection helps learn complex tasks over a handful of trials
LeetcodeHardGym: 40 hard Leetcode questions in 19 programming languages
Improvements over strong baselines and state-of-the-art on several code generation benchmarks

method.summary: Three LLM roles (Actor, Evaluator, Self-Reflection) loop over trials: the Actor acts, the Evaluator scores the trajectory (exact match, heuristic, LLM classifier or self-written unit tests), the Self-Reflection model writes a verbal lesson appended to a bounded memory that is fed to the Actor next trial. No weights are updated.
method.task: Sequential decision-making (ALFWorld), multi-hop QA (HotPotQA), code generation (HumanEval, MBPP, LeetcodeHardGym)

datasets.name: HumanEval (Python, Rust)

datasets.name: LeetcodeHardGym

inference.samples: Trials per task until success or max trials: ALFWorld 12 consecutive trials; HotPotQA retry until 3 consecutive failed attempts; WebShop 4 trials; Table 4 averaged over 8 trials; other runs not stated
inference.prompting: ALFWorld: ReAct, 2 few-shot trajectories; HotPotQA: CoT 6-shot, ReAct 2-shot, self-reflection 2-shot; code: zero-shot instruction, Actor/Self-reflection prompts in Appendix C

parameters.alfworld_reflect_trigger: same action and same response for more than 3 cycles, or more than 30 actions in an environment
parameters.max_trials: not stated as a single number

other.evaluator: HotPotQA exact match; ALFWorld heuristic or GPT binary classification; programming self-generated unit tests

metrics.name: Pass@1

metrics.name: Proportion of solved tasks/environments by trial

prompts.text: You are a Python writing assistant. You will be given your previous implementation of a function, a series of unit tests results, and your self-reflection on your previous implementation. Apply the necessary changes below by responding only with the improved body of the function. Do not include the signature in your response. The first line of your response should have 4 spaces of indentation so that it fits syntactically with the user provided signature. You will be given a few examples by the user.

limits: Relies on the LLM's self-evaluation or heuristics; no formal guarantee of success
May get stuck in local minima; WebShop showed no improvement after 4 trials (Appendix B.1)
Memory is only a sliding window of 1-3 reflections; vector or SQL memory left to future work
Unit-test self-evaluation fails for non-deterministic, impure, hardware-dependent or concurrent functions; false positives hurt MBPP Python
Self-correction is emergent in stronger models: starchat-beta shows no gain (Appendix A)
Models were GPT-3/3.5/4 API versions of 2023; no seeds, variance or compute cost reported for most results
Generated code is executed unvalidated; use isolated environments
